name: Cover crops
action: Establish non-cash cover crops (such as legumes, grasses, or brassicas) during fallow or inter-row periods to maintain living ground cover.
mechanism: Living roots maintain rhizosphere microbial activity and mycorrhizal networks throughout the year, reduce raindrop impact detachment, and cycle organic matter into topsoil.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Continuous living root exudates and plant biomass cycle active carbon into topsoil horizons.
Vegetative canopy and surface roots intercept raindrops and physically anchor topsoil.
Rhizosphere root exudation supports bacterial and mycorrhizal fungal populations.

confidence.label: High Confidence
confidence.basis: FAO Global Soil Partnership, CSIRO dryland reviews

trade_offs: In water-limited environments (<350 mm annual precipitation), terminate cover crops early to avoid excessive soil moisture depletion before cash crop sowing.

name: Field margins
action: Establish uncropped perennial vegetation buffers, native flowering hedgerows, and grass strips along parcel boundaries and field borders.
mechanism: Permanent field margins provide undisturbed nesting habitat and alternative floral resources for native pollinators and predatory beneficial arthropods, suppressing pest outbreaks naturally.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Permanent floral resources and undisturbed ground nesting habitat support wild pollinators.
Perennial vegetation provides refugia for predatory arthropods and beneficial insects.
Linear border vegetation creates wildlife movement corridors across fragmented agricultural matrix.

trade_offs: Takes a minor percentage of field border area out of direct crop production; requires monitoring for weed encroachment.

name: Crop rotation
action: Diversify single-crop systems by alternating cereal crops with pulses, oilseeds, or deep-rooting species across successive seasons.
mechanism: Varying root architectures and root exudates disrupt pest and disease cycles, optimize nutrient uptake from distinct soil layers, and enhance biological diversity.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Alternating functional plant types diversifies root exudates and reduces nutrient exhaustion.
Non-host rotational crops break species-specific weed, pest, and disease reproductive cycles.
Diverse cropping profiles mitigate climatic and economic risks compared to monoculture.

confidence.label: High Confidence
confidence.basis: FAO and ICRISAT long-term trial meta-analyses

trade_offs: Requires market access and suitable harvesting or processing equipment for rotational crops.

name: Residue retention
action: Leave crop stubble and plant residues on the field surface after harvest rather than burning, removing, or burying them.
mechanism: Surface residue creates a physical mulch barrier that buffers soil temperature extremes, suppresses evaporative moisture loss, and shields soil aggregates from wind and water erosion.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Surface mulch reduces direct solar radiation on soil, lowering evaporative water loss.
Stubble blanket dampens peak daytime topsoil temperatures, protecting surface biology.
Residue protects surface aggregates from kinetic raindrop impact and wind detachment.

confidence.label: High Confidence
confidence.basis: IPCC Climate Change and Land, FAO Conservation Agriculture

trade_offs: Heavy residue may interfere with standard seed drills if specialized seeders are unavailable; can harbor crop-specific fungal residues if not rotated.

name: Agroforestry
action: Integrate multipurpose perennial woody species and shelterbelts alongside seasonal crops at appropriate spatial configurations.
mechanism: Tree canopies reduce near-surface wind speeds and evaporative demand, while deep perennial root systems access subsoil moisture and nutrients, recycling organic matter via litterfall.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Perennial boundary trees slow near-surface wind speeds and dampen vapor pressure deficit.
Deep roots capture subsoil nutrients, returning them to the topsoil through annual leaf litter.
Vertical woody canopy layers provide perches, nesting sites, and micro-refugia for native fauna.

confidence.label: High Confidence
confidence.basis: FAO Agroforestry guidelines, ICRAF global synthesis

trade_offs: Requires multi-year investment before tree canopies mature; tree species must be selected to avoid light or moisture competition with companion crops.

name: Reduced tillage
action: Minimize or eliminate mechanical inversion tillage (moldboard plowing) in favor of direct drilling, strip-till, or shallow non-inversion cultivation.
mechanism: Avoiding soil inversion preserves soil pore architecture, earthworm channels, and fungal hyphae networks, reducing carbon oxidation and mitigating compaction.

impacted_metrics.causal_mechanism: Undisturbed fungal hyphae and earthworm burrows maintain soil macropores and water infiltration.
Minimizing soil disturbance limits oxygen exposure, decreasing oxidative loss of organic matter.
Fewer tractor passes reduce fossil fuel consumption and subsoil plow-pan compaction.

confidence.label: High Confidence
confidence.basis: FAO Conservation Agriculture, Global Soil Partnership

trade_offs: Transition period (1-3 years) may require adjusted weed management strategies before soil biology establishes equilibrium.
